title: Federal Reserve raises rates by half a point
body: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by half a percentage point on Wednesday to a range of 5.5 to 5.75 percent, its largest increase this year. Chair Elena Ruiz said inflation remained too high and that the committee was prepared to move again in September if price pressures did not ease. Two members of the committee dissented in favour of a quarter-point move. Stocks fell after the announcement, with the S&P 500 closing down 1.4 percent.

title: Fed delivers biggest hike of the year as inflation stays hot
body: The Federal Open Market Committee lifted the federal funds target range by 50 basis points to 5.50 to 5.75 percent on Wednesday, the largest step since 2023. In her press conference, chair Elena Ruiz said recent inflation readings were "unacceptably high" and left open a further increase at the September meeting. The vote was 10 to 2, with governors Sam Lindqvist and Maria Costa preferring a quarter-point rise. Treasury yields rose across the curve.

title: Mortgage applications fall 12 percent after rate rise
body: Applications for home loans fell 12 percent in the week to August 15, the Mortgage Lenders Council said on Wednesday, as the average 30-year fixed rate climbed to 7.4 percent following the Federal Reserve's half-point increase earlier this month. Refinancing applications dropped 19 percent and purchase applications 8 percent. The council's chief economist, Grace Okonjo, said the decline was the sharpest weekly fall since 2022. Council economists expect applications to keep falling through the autumn.
